newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL - Italy May PPI, WPI seen up, but not worrying.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Italy May PPI, WPI seen up, but not worrying.

text.p: Italian producer and wholesale prices are both expected to post a slight month on month rise in May due to an increase in oil prices but the upturn is not seen as particularly worrying, analysts said.
The PPI and WPI data will be released at 0700 GMT on Tuesday, July 15.
A Reuter survey of 10 economists showed on average May PPI rising 0.1 percent month-on-month and by a yearly 1.1 percent.
In April, PPI was zero on a monthly basis and 0.8 percent year on year. In May 1996, prices fell 0.2 percent month on month but rose by 1.3 percent year on year.
On average, May wholesale prices were seen rising 0.1 percent month on month but falling an annual 0.3 percent.
In April, WPI fell 0.4 percent monthly and by 0.7 percent year on year. In May 1996, prices fell 0.3 percent month on month but rose by 3.5 percent annually.
"In the last few months the oil price had a determining effect on the lower trend in PPI and WPI but in May this should come to a halt," said Lucia Trevisan of Caboto brokers.

Lorenzo Codogno of Bank of America noted that domestic demand in the second quarter was stronger than expected and "therefore there could be a small sign in May companies are ready to pass some wage increases on to consumers."
Paolo Casadio of Credito Italiano said that the increase in oil prices would be counterbalanced by a decline in other commodity prices.

Some analysts noted however that May could be the last month in which the year on year PPI rise was around 1.0 percent and that in the next three months, due to an unfavourable statistical comparison with 1996 months, could almost double.

Gianluca Sanna of Stone & McCarthy said that even if a monthly rise of just 0.1 percent for the next three months was forecast, "we would nevertheless see a July year on year increase of near 1.8 percent from the current 0.8 percent. But this rise doesn't mean anything in terms of the effective dynamics of inflation."
